assertions_contracts.best_practice: Consistent with the handbook's narrowing documentation the guide cites; TS 6/7 did not change assertion-signature semantics.
assertions_contracts.evidence: No assertion-model change in the 6.0 release notes or the 7.0 announcement.
assertions_contracts.guide_position: User-defined assertion signatures must actually test and narrow unknown; never use ! or casts to bypass external validation; console.assert does not terminate; internal invariant failures may throw, expected failures use the declared result contract.

bounded_work.best_practice: No official TypeScript/Node source prescribes budgets; nothing contradicts bounded admission. TS 7's parallel checker is a compiler-internal change and does not relax application-level bounding.
bounded_work.evidence: Stricter-than-mainstream Tiger policy; no contradicting official position found in the 6.0 notes or 7.0 announcement.
bounded_work.guide_position: Named *_MAX bounds for item count, item size, nesting, cumulative bytes, concurrent and waiting work, elapsed time and retry amplification; retries need idempotency, a shared deadline, bounded backoff and injected jitter.

concurrency.best_practice: AbortSignal-based cancellation remains the platform idiom in current Node/Web docs; TS 7 changes compiler parallelism (--checkers/--builders), not the application async model.
concurrency.evidence: 7.0 announcement's parallelization flags concern tsc itself; application concurrency rules are untouched by 6.0/7.0.
concurrency.guide_position: Pass AbortSignal where supported; Promise.race timeout is not cancellation; bounded task registry; abort owned work on teardown and await settlement; reject stale results before commit; workers for CPU isolation with separate shared-memory policy.

error_handling.best_practice: No official source prescribes Result vs exceptions; both remain in mainstream use and TS 6/7 made no change here. Handling thrown values as unknown matches strict-mode useUnknownInCatchVariables behaviour.
error_handling.evidence: Neither the 6.0 release notes nor the 7.0 announcement alter catch-variable or error semantics.
error_handling.guide_position: Discriminated Result<T,E> for expected failures (or the subsystem's declared contract), typed thrown errors handled at one boundary, catch values as unknown, every started promise awaited or owned, causes preserved, secrets redacted from serialized errors.

formatting.best_practice: Current practice has consolidated: Biome is a single formatter+linter (its official site ships migrate commands from both ESLint and Prettier), while ESLint+Prettier remains the two-tool stack. What no current source supports is the guide's muddle: SKILL names prettier+biome, the operating rules say 'prettier + eslint', and the validation recipe runs prettier and eslint but never biome.
formatting.evidence: Biome's official migration doc treats biome as the replacement for ESLint and/or Prettier in one config, confirming biome in the pairing line occupies the lint+format slot the guide elsewhere gives to eslint.
formatting.guide_position: SKILL toolchain pairing says 'prettier and biome for formatting'; operating rules say one pinned formatter and lint profile '(e.g. prettier + eslint)'; guide Section 23 says one pinned formatter and lint profile; guide Section 27 validation runs prettier --check and eslint, with no biome command anywhere.

memory_ownership.best_practice: Ownership/bounding claims remain sound; the guide's disposal hedge predates the current baseline but is conditional rather than wrong, so this is not scored stale - see proposals.
memory_ownership.evidence: No official 6.0/7.0 change affects the guide's retention or admission claims.
memory_ownership.guide_position: Bound maps/caches/strings/buffers/queued promises/worker messages; Promise.all starts all work eagerly so bound admission before creating promises; short views can retain large ArrayBuffers; one owner per resource with try/finally dispose/close; FinalizationRegistry is not cleanup; disposal syntax only where runtime/toolchain support is verified.

security.best_practice: Aligns with current Node child_process guidance the guide cites; the type system remains non-sandboxing. TS 6/7 introduce no contrary guidance.
security.evidence: Guide cites the Node child_process API docs directly; no 2026 change to those security semantics was found in the sources fetched.
security.guide_position: Never eval/new Function on untrusted data; no innerHTML for text; type checker is not a sandbox; argv-form spawn/execFile with shell:false; path normalization is not authorization and startsWith is not containment; temp file in destination dir then rename; committed lockfile with frozen CI installs; review install scripts/native addons.

static_analysis.best_practice: TS 7.0 ships with no programmatic compiler API (a new API is expected in 7.1), so API-consuming analysis tooling such as typescript-eslint cannot run against TS 7 directly; Microsoft's documented pattern is a side-by-side install: TS 7's tsc for checking, with the @typescript/typescript6 compatibility package aliased in for API consumers.
static_analysis.evidence: The 7.0 announcement's side-by-side section names typescript-eslint explicitly as a tool that still needs the 6.0 API and documents the npm-alias pattern with @typescript/typescript6.
static_analysis.guide_position: Gate on tsc --noEmit plus a pinned lint profile; guide validation recipe runs ./node_modules/.bin/eslint . unconditionally, with no mention of which TypeScript version the lint stack consumes.

testing.best_practice: Nothing in TS 6/7 changes this; testing emitted JS remains necessary because type stripping/erasure behaviour is unchanged in the native port (7.0 is a faithful port of 6.0 semantics).
testing.evidence: 7.0 announcement describes the port as deliberately faithful to 6.0 structure and results.
testing.guide_position: Decoder tests over null/undefined/booleans/fractional/NaN/infinity/unsafe integers/sparse arrays/oversize/prototype-like keys; rejection also tested under emitted JavaScript; half validation / half adversarial split.

toolchain_pins.best_practice: Current release is TypeScript 7.0 (7.0.2), the native Go port, GA 2026-07-08, roughly 8-12x faster on full builds. TS 6.0 (Mar 2026) was the last JavaScript-codebase release and the bridge: it turned strict on by default, defaulted types to [], defaulted module to esnext and target to the latest ES version, and deprecated baseUrl, node10/classic module resolution, target es5 and several module kinds - all of which TS 7 turns into hard errors. @typescript/native-preview (the tsgo preview) is superseded; nightlies ship as typescript@next.
toolchain_pins.evidence: Official 7.0 announcement fetched in full (speedups, no-API caveat, side-by-side package, native-preview superseded). Official 6.0 release notes document the baseUrl deprecation and the changed defaults.
toolchain_pins.guide_position: Pin TypeScript 5.9+ with an ES2022 target; guide header and Section 2 declare a 'TypeScript 5.9-compatible strict profile'; strict profile options are enumerated explicitly (good), but no 6.x/7.x defaults, deprecations or the native compiler are mentioned.

current_versions.@typescript/native-preview: Superseded/frozen at 7.0 dev builds; nightlies now ship as typescript@next - the 'tsgo' name in the skill is preview-era
current_versions.biome: Current single-binary formatter+linter (Biome 2.x line) with official migrate commands from ESLint and Prettier
current_versions.eslint/typescript-eslint: Still the type-aware lint stack, but under TS 7 it must consume the TypeScript 6 API via the @typescript/typescript6 compatibility package (no programmatic API in TS 7.0; new API expected in 7.1)
current_versions.prettier: Still maintained as a formatter-only tool; guide's pairing muddle (prettier+biome vs prettier+eslint) is internal, not a Prettier status change
current_versions.typescript: 7.0.2 current stable (native Go port, GA 2026-07-08); 6.0.3 is the last JavaScript-codebase release and the supported sidecar for API consumers
current_versions.typescript-language-server (ts_ls): Community LSP wrapper around the TS 6 API; TS 7 ships its own native language server - ts_ls remains usable only against the 6.x API surface

mechanical_fixes.correct: TypeScript 7.0+ (native compiler; 6.0 retained only as the API sidecar for tooling) and a current ES target (ES2025-era; set target/rootDir/types explicitly)
mechanical_fixes.evidence: TypeScript 7.0 is the current stable release (7.0.2, GA 2026-07-08); 6.0 was the last release from the JavaScript codebase and 5.9 is two majors behind.

mechanical_fixes.correct: **Primary target:** TypeScript 7.0 strict profile (6.0 API sidecar where tooling requires it); ES2025+
mechanical_fixes.evidence: Same as above: 7.0 is current, 6.0 the bridge release, 5.9 superseded.

mechanical_fixes.correct: a TypeScript 7.0 strict profile (with the 6.0 compatibility package only where a tool consumes the compiler API)
mechanical_fixes.current: a TypeScript 5.9-compatible strict profile and ES2022
mechanical_fixes.evidence: Same as above; a '5.9-compatible' profile also silently inherits pre-6.0 defaults that 6.0 changed and 7.0 enforces.

mechanical_fixes.correct: typescript-language-server (ts_ls against the 6.x API, or TypeScript 7's bundled native language server; deno_ls for Deno)
mechanical_fixes.evidence: tsgo was the binary of the @typescript/native-preview package; the 7.0 announcement states that package is superseded, nightlies resume under typescript@next, and TS 7 ships its own tsc/language server - there is no current tsgo_ls pairing.

proposals.evidence: The 7.0 announcement's side-by-side section documents exactly this alias pattern, names typescript-eslint as the motivating consumer, and states a new API is expected in 7.1.
proposals.proposal: Adopt the documented dual-install: pin typescript@^7.0.2 as the checking compiler (native tsc) and alias typescript to npm:@typescript/typescript6 for API consumers (typescript-eslint and any custom transformers), with CI running the native tsc as the authoritative gate. State in the guide that a type a native check rejects can still look green in an editor resolving through the 6.x alias.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt now; drop the sidecar only when the lint stack runs on the 7.1 API.

proposals.evidence: 6.0 release notes deprecate baseUrl (no longer a resolution root) and the December 2025 TS7 progress post lists the changed defaults (strict on, target floats to latest ES, rootDir = tsconfig directory) and the options 7.0 removes.
proposals.proposal: Rebuild the Section 23 example tsconfig for the 6/7 world: write every load-bearing option explicitly (the guide's own philosophy), set rootDir and types explicitly instead of inheriting the new defaults, use nodenext or bundler resolution, and add a short 'removed in 7.0, never use' list (baseUrl, node10/classic resolution, target es5, amd/umd/systemjs modules, outFile, esModuleInterop:false).
proposals.recommendation: Adopt with the version re-pin; keep the CommonJS standalone-example note but mark it as an example-local exception.

proposals.evidence: Biome's official site ships migrate commands from both ESLint and Prettier into a single biome.json, i.e. biome replaces the pair rather than complementing Prettier.
proposals.proposal: Pick exactly one format/lint stack and make SKILL, operating rules and the validation recipe agree: either Biome alone (format+lint+organize-imports in one pinned binary) or Prettier (format) + ESLint/typescript-eslint (lint). The current text names prettier+biome in the pairing line, prettier+eslint in the rules, and runs prettier+eslint in the recipe.
proposals.recommendation: For Matt's Neovim-first, low-dependency bias, pilot Biome-only on one project and keep ESLint only where type-aware rules are load-bearing (those need the TS6 sidecar anyway).
